# Tests that fail on the upstream commit in `upstream-base` on a GitHub-hosted
# Linux runner, and still fail on the fork. The fork's CI leaves them out,
# because their failure is not the fork's to fix.
#
# Regenerate after every update from upstream: push the new upstream commit
# plus `.github/` to a `ci-baseline/` branch, push the updated fork to a second
# `ci-baseline/` branch, take the failed-test list from the summary of each
# full-suite job, and keep the entries that fail on both. One test per line:
# nextest binary id, a space, the test name.
#
# Source: upstream 9e9dbb897e91ed043d3ad1924444639d2d1979c6, run
# https://github.com/silvarbor/mcp_agent_mail_rust/actions/runs/43700208425,
# compared with the fork at bdc2b0a8, run
# https://github.com/silvarbor/mcp_agent_mail_rust/actions/runs/43700208547.

# Kept by hand: keep this entry when regenerating the list above.
#
# Intermittent on both platforms, so the two baseline runs need not show it.
# The test starts 16 and then 32 writers on one database and usually ends in
# about 22 seconds. In run 43767180406 it reached the 240-second limit in both
# attempts on macOS, on code that had passed in 23 seconds an hour earlier. On
# a Mac, 2 of 8 rounds with `AM_TEST_WRITER_STORM_TRACE=1` timed out the same
# way: after every other writer has finished, one writer's INSERT waits 20
# seconds inside the database engine and returns "database is busy (snapshot
# conflict on pages: 109)", attempt after attempt. The engine and the retry
# wrapper are upstream's; the fork changes neither. Upstream records the same
# timeout twice (upstream commit 30dbc925). Drop the entry when upstream has
# fixed it.
mcp-agent-mail-db queries::tests::autocommit_writer_storm_loses_no_rows_and_keeps_integrity
